title: Rewrite or patch the billing reconciliation service?

provenance.author: hand
provenance.license: synthetic-fixture: fully fictional, no real persons or private data
provenance.notes: Three-speaker engineering decision. Authored as a Tier-1 ground-truth fixture. Contains a root-cause crux, a tangent (espresso machine), a genuine reversal/surprise, three action items, and a rebuts/supports/clarify edge mix.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Okay, billing sync. Do we rewrite the reconciliation service or keep patching it? I want a decision today.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Patching is bleeding us. We've shipped fourteen hotfixes to that one service in the last quarter alone.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Fourteen? I knew it was bad, but I didn't realize it was that bad.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: The core issue is the schema. It assumes one currency per account, and we now have multi-currency customers. That assumption is the root of basically every reconciliation bug.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Exactly, and a clean rewrite lets us model currency as a first-class dimension instead of bolting it on. I think we should just rewrite it.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: I hear you, but a full rewrite means no new billing features for a quarter. From the customer side, that freeze is a very real cost.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Fair. Although, unrelated, did the new espresso machine ever get fixed? Half the team's been on instant coffee for two weeks and morale is visibly down.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Facilities said Thursday. Anyway, sorry, back to billing.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: So what if we strangler-fig it instead? Wrap the old service, route only multi-currency accounts to a new module, and leave single-currency accounts on the old path for now.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Huh. That actually surprises me as the right call. I walked in here assuming a full rewrite was the only clean fix, but this avoids the freeze.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: The risk is two code paths to maintain during the migration window. That overhead isn't free, and bugs love seams like that.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Sure, but it's bounded. We delete the old path the moment everyone's migrated, and customers never see a feature freeze. The seam is temporary by design.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Okay, I'm convinced. Strangler-fig it, multi-currency module first. That's the decision.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Action items: Sam, you scaffold the new module and the routing layer by next Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: On it. I'll also write the migration runbook so the cutover isn't tribal knowledge.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: And I'll socialize the no-feature-freeze message with our three biggest accounts so nobody's caught off guard.

claims.text: Fourteen hotfixes shipped to the reconciliation service last quarter
The billing schema assumes one currency per account
We should rewrite the reconciliation service
